content: STEP 1 — goal: scope/spec audit of the five proposals against the contract (behaviour signal, curved op, real coupling, three switches, derived constants, one-run cost). Read: the five proposal texts and the per-idea evidence bundles (BEHAVIORAL_EVIDENCE E1-E3 PROPOSED, GEOMETRIC_NECESSITY E12-E13 PROPOSED, plus shared OBSERVED E5-E11). Observed: all five pass the scope gate (each names a training-only transition-demand signal, an explicit exp_0/Mobius/artanh Poincare distance in the level-1 argmin, and both switches that reduce EXACTLY to baseline: behaviour-off -> offset 0, geometry-off -> c=0 -> Euclidean). Differences that matter for ranking: (a) COUPLING DEPTH — closed per-step loop (demand measured through the same curved soft assignment then subtracted from that curved distance) in l1pdo-rq, DEMARGIN-L1-CURV and BEABLATE-CURVSCALE; frozen pre-computed tables in pmi-geomargin-l1-rq and GEOMARGIN-L1-RQ. (b) CONSTANT HYGIENE — offset scale measured in the same units as d_c in DEMARGIN (mean geodesic half-margin) and BEABLATE (0.25*s_D, s_D = mean min_k D_k), 0.10 of an epoch-1 measured scale in pmi and 0.10*Dbar/rms(z) in GEOMARGIN, but l1pdo uses w = beta = 0.25, the baseline commitment weight that multiplies a SQUARED residual, applied to a length — dimensionally borrowed. (c) STABILITY — l1pdo's offset is centred and clipped to +/-ln3*0.25 (bounded, symmetric); DEMARGIN's is one-sided, clamp[0,3w] on a mean-normalised heavy-tailed demand; BEABLATE's EMA lambda = 1/72000 over a 72,000-step budget leaves demand near 1 for most of training. Still open: which of these differences the frozen evidence actually rewards.

STEP 2 — goal: ground each proposal in the shared OBSERVED evidence. Read: E5-E11 of every bundle (identical content). Observations: E6/E7 beam survival and teacher-forced NLL: the hyperbolic level-1 variant l1_br already DEGENERATED in the probes (T1 NLL 0.00, T4 NLL 9.03, recall@10 0.04671), while Euclidean level-1 variants reached l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233 and the best observed 0.06363 (resample, which buys its gain at depth 3-4: T3 NLL 0.73, T4 0.05, gold prefix alive depth4 0.088). So (i) a level-1-only mechanism inherits a family base rate that has so far failed to pass 0.065, and (ii) the documented failure mode of a curved level-1 assignment is first-token mass collapse (T1 NLL = 0.00), which one-sided/unbounded demand attractors risk repeating. E6 also shows gold-prefix survival at depth 1 is already 1.000 for l1_br_euclid/l1_only, so the gain must come from compressing levels 2-3, not from token-1 accuracy. E8: share of canonical pairs sharing a K=256 level-1 code is only 0.0822 (permuted -0.0129) against 0.3106 at K=16 -> there IS headroom for behaviour-aligned level-1 co-location; E11: same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067 shows the current prefix carries almost no behavioural information. E5/E10: demand is highly skewed (top-1 successor mass 0.4375 in the low-entropy quintile; mean out-degree 5.45, median branch 3), which is the concrete argument for popularity adjustment and against unbounded offsets. Still open: final ordering.

STEP 3 — final answer (complete, stands alone).

RANK: l1pdo-rq | position=1 | reason=Only proposal combining a genuine closed geometry->behaviour->geometry loop (per-codeword demand built from the same curved softmax whose distance the offset then shifts) with a bounded, mean-centred offset (clipped at +/-ln3*0.25), which is the form the evidence says is needed: E7 shows the curved level-1 arm l1_br collapsed first-token mass (T1 NLL 0.00, recall 0.04671), so a symmetric bounded offset is the safest way to use the level-1 headroom of E8 (0.0822 of canonical pairs share a K=256 code vs 0.3106 at K=16) without repeating that collapse; its one defect is w = beta = 0.25 borrowed from the squared-residual commitment term.
RANK: DEMARGIN-L1-CURV | position=2 | reason=Same closed loop and the best-derived offset scale of the five (w = measured mean geodesic half-margin, T = w, both in the units actually subtracted from d_c), so the behaviour/geometry balance is not an arbitrary constant; but its offset is one-sided, clamp[0,3w] on a mean-normalised demand that E5/E10 show is heavy-tailed (top-1 successor mass 0.4375, mean out-degree 5.45), which is exactly the hub-attractor that produced the l1_br degeneration in E7; ranked second, not first, on that stability difference alone.
RANK: pmi-geomargin-l1-rq | position=3 | reason=Its behaviour statistic is the best matched to the evidence — a degree-normalised (PMI-style) transition surplus, which directly counters the hub dominance visible in E5/E10 and the near-chance behavioural content of the prefix in E11 (0.0907 vs permuted 0.067), and its offset is bounded at 0.10 of a measured epoch-1 scale; it drops below the closed-loop pair because b_k is a frozen table so the geometry never feeds back into the behaviour term, and c = (0.5/s)^2 puts typical items at ball norm ~0.46, i.e. close to the Euclidean regime its own risk list flags.
RANK: GEOMARGIN-L1-RQ | position=4 | reason=Cleanest switch algebra of the five (zero-mean margin, so behaviour-off is literally the baseline argmin) and a derived weight w = 0.1*Dbar/rms(z); but z is built in a frozen pre-pass from frozen hard level-1 assignments, so the coupling is single-shot and stale relative to the moving encoder (its own stated risk), and the margin cap of 10% of the typical geodesic distance is the kind of nudge that E6/E7's flat 0.0550 successor_geodesic_coarse and tangent_successor_residual results suggest does not move recall.
RANK: BEABLATE-CURVSCALE-RQ | position=5 | reason=Dimensionally the tidiest offset (w*s_D with s_D the measured mean min_k D_k, hence curvature-invariant) but lambda = 1/72000 over the frozen 72,000-step budget leaves demand within a few percent of 1 for most of training and caps the competing part of the offset at 0.25*s_D, with c = 0.25 placing typical ball norm at ~0.23 (near-Euclidean); that makes it the arm most likely to be statistically indistinguishable from baseline in a single run, which E6's 0.0555-0.0638 spread says is fatal for a 0.065 target.

OBJECTION: All five proposals act only on the level-1 argmin, yet the frozen evidence shows the gold level-1 prefix is already alive at depth 1 for the Euclidean level-1 variants (1.000 for l1_br_euclid/l1_only, E6) and that the observed recall spread is won or lost at depths 3-4 (resample 0.06363 with T3/T4 NLL 0.73/0.05, E7), so the round's mechanism may be capped below 0.065 by attacking a non-binding constraint; and the one curved level-1 arm already run (l1_
br) degenerated to T1 NLL 0.00 / recall 0.04671, so any one-sided demand offset risks reproducing that collapse and a single run cannot separate that failure from seed noise.
